rubric_fields.label: Originalidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Identifique a contribuição e diferencie-a de conhecimento já estabelecido. Exija evidência no artigo para a alegação de novidade, sem presumir que novidade implique qualidade.

rubric_fields.label: Solidez
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confronte conclusões com métodos, dados ou demonstrações apresentados. Verifique hipóteses, limitações e se o desenho permite a inferência alegada; adapte a exigência ao tipo de artigo.

rubric_fields.label: Substância
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique se experimentos, provas, síntese ou análise sustentam a contribuição declarada. Considere a profundidade e a cobertura da evidência, sem confundir extensão do texto com substância.

rubric_fields.label: Clareza
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique definições, organização e correspondência entre texto, tabelas e figuras. Aponte ambiguidades localizáveis e distinga problemas de redação de problemas científicos.

rubric_fields.label: Comparação
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confira se os trabalhos e alternativas relevantes são discutidos de forma justa. Compare métodos, condições e limitações equivalentes; não exija experimentos de um artigo estritamente teórico.

rubric_fields.label: Impacto
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Relacione a contribuição a uma necessidade da área e ao alcance sustentado pelos resultados. Distinga relevância demonstrada de aplicações futuras ainda especulativas.

rubric_fields.label: Reprodutibilidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique disponibilidade ou descrição suficiente de materiais, dados, procedimentos e parâmetros. Restrições éticas ou legais podem justificar acesso controlado; não exija divulgação de dados pessoais.

document_map.abstract:
The accuracy of Japanese predicate ar-gument structure (PAS) analysis has im-proved in recent years thanks to jointmodeling of interactions between multiplepredicates. However, this approach heav-ily relies on syntactic information pre-dicted by parsers, and suffers from theerror propagation. To remedy this prob-lem, we introduce a model using grid-typer
recurrent neural networks (Grid-RNN),which automatically induces features sen-sitive to multi-predicate interactions fromword sequence information of a sentence.The experiments on the NAIST Text Cor-pus show that our model exceeds the accu-racy of the state-of-the-art Japanese PASanalyzer without syntactic information.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.first_sentence: Predicate argument structure (PAS) analysis is a basic semantic analysis task, in which systems are required to identify semantic units of a sentence, such as who did what to whom.

sections.title: 2.1 Task Description
sections.first_sentence: In Japanese PAS analysis, we identify arguments taking part in the three major case roles, nominative (NOM), accusative (ACC) and dative (DAT) cases, for each predicate.

sections.title: 2.2 Challenging Problem
sections.first_sentence: Arguments are often omitted in Japanese sen-tences.

sections.title: 3 Single-Sequence Model
sections.first_sentence: The single-sequence model exploits stacked bidirectional RNNs (Bi-RNN) (Schuster and Paliwal, 1997; Graves et al., 2005, 2013; Zhou and Xu, 2015).

sections.title: 3.1 Input Layer
sections.first_sentence:
Given an input sentence W1:T = (w1,……,wT) and a predicate p, each word wt is mapped to a feature representation xt, which is the concatena- tion (⊕) of three types of vectors:

xt = xargt ⊕ xpredt ⊕ xmarkt

where each vector is based on the following atomic features inspired by Zhou and Xu (2015):

ARG: Word index of each word.

sections.title: 3.2 RNN Layer
sections.first_sentence: In the RNN layers, feature vectors are updated recurrently using Bi-RNNs.

sections.title: 3.3 Output Layer
sections.first_sentence:
In the output layer, multi-class classification is performed using the softmax function:

yt = softmax(Wy h(L))

where h(L) is a vector representation propagated from the last RNN layer (Fig 3).

sections.title: 4 Multi-Sequence Model
sections.first_sentence: While the single-sequence model assumes the independence between predicates, the multi-sequence model assumes the multi-predicate interactions.

sections.title: 4.1 Input Layer
sections.first_sentence: The multi-sequence model takes as input a sen- tence W1:T = (w1,……,wτ) and all predicates {pm} in the sentence.

sections.title: 4.2 Grid Layer
sections.first_sentence: In the grid layers, we use Grid-RNNs to propa- gate the feature information over the different se- quences (inter-sequence connections).

sections.title: 4.3 Output Layer
sections.first_sentence:
Like the single-sequence model, using the softmax function, we calculate the probability of case la- bels of each word wt for each predicate pm:

ym,t = softmax(Wy h(L)m,t)

where h(L)m,t is a hidden state vector calculated in the last Grid Layer.

sections.title: 5.1 Japanese PAS Analysis Approaches
sections.first_sentence: Existing approaches for Japanese PAS analysis are divided into two categories: (i) pointwise ap- proach and (ii) joint approach.

sections.title: 5.2 Multi-Predicate Interactions

sections.title: Japanese PAS
sections.first_sentence: In recent years, several attempts have been made to apply neural networks for Japanese PAS analysis (Shibata et al., 2016; Iida et al., 2016).

sections.title: English SRL
sections.first_sentence: Some neural models achieved high perfor-mance without syntactic information in En-glish SRL.

sections.title: Dataset
sections.first_sentence: We use the NAIST Text Corpus 1.5, which con-sists of 40,000 sentences of Japanese newspapertext (Iida et al., 2007).

sections.title: Learning
sections.first_sentence:
We train the model parameters by minimizing the cross-entropy loss function:

C(0) = - ΣΣ log P(Yt/Pr) + 1/||0||2

where @ is a set of model parameters, and the hyper-parameter A is the coefficient governing the L2 weight decay.

sections.title: Implementation Details
sections.first_sentence: We implement our neural models using Theano (Bastien et al., 2012).

sections.title: Neural Models vs Baseline Models
sections.first_sentence: Table 1 presents F-measures of our neural se- quence models with 8 RNN or Grid layers and the baseline models on the test set, in which as the significent test, we used the bootstrap resampling method.

sections.title: Effects of Multiple Predicate Consideration
sections.first_sentence: As Table 1 shows, the multi-sequence model significantly outperformed the single-sequence model in F-measure in total (81.42% vs 81.15%).

sections.title: 7 Conclusion
sections.first_sentence: In this work, we introduced neural sequence mod- els that automatically induce effective feature rep- resentations from word sequence information of a sentence for Japanese PAS analysis.
